question: Philosophia Naturalis Principia Mathematica, popularly known as Principia, published in 1687, is the greatest work of which scientist?
solution:
The correct answer is **Isaac Newton.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Isaac Newton in his book** Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687).**
 
• His law of general attractive energy in three books written in Latin, first distributed** 5 July 1687.**
 
• The Principia structures the groundwork of traditional** mechanics.**
 
• The Principia is viewed as quite possibly of the main work throughout the entire existence of science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Johannes Kepler** was a German cosmologist, mathematician, soothsayer, regular logician essayist on music.
 
• **John Philoponus** otherwise called John the Grammarian or John of Alexandria.
 
• **Edmond **was an English stargazer, geophysicist, mathematician, meteorologist, and physicist.** In 1718,** he found the appropriate movement of the "fixed" stars.
 
• **Isaac Newton** is best know for his theory about the law of gravity, but his “Principia Mathematica” **(1686) **with its three laws of motion greatly influenced the Enlightenment in Europe.
